primary_intent: Create and save a single new Triage encounter for patient p1 with the exact note provided, without making any other changes. A reasonable user would be inflexible about the encounter actually being saved (committed); attempting without a successful save would not satisfy the request.
reasoning: Nitpicks: None — the agent used the correct app, opened patient p1, set type to Triage, and entered the exact note. Critical issues: The encounter was not saved due to an HTTP 409 error, so the primary deliverable (a saved encounter) is missing. Critical-Point rules: With permission granted, success requires completing the binding save action. Here, an environment blocker (HTTP 409) prevented completing the save, so this matches the failure rule for environment prevention of the binding action. Outcome: Screenshots confirm 'Encounter for patient p1' with Type=Triage and the exact note, but also show 'Save failed (error 409)'. The agent reported this accurately, made no extraneous changes, and clicked save once — however, the result (a saved encounter) was not achieved. A reasonable user would not consider this successful.

items.criterion: Use the clinic's record app as the platform
items.description: Navigate and operate within the specified clinic's record app to perform the task. Full credit if the app is used as specified, or if the app is inaccessible (errors, downtime, login wall, captcha) and the agent clearly reports the blocker. Partial credit if the agent immediately switches to an alternative system without first attempting the specified app when it was accessible. Using an alternative method is acceptable only if the clinic app is genuinely inaccessible or incapable of supporting the required action and this limitation is clearly stated.
items.justification: All actions occurred on http://clinic.example within the clinic app (new-encounter form and save attempt). No alternative platform was used; a server error was reported.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows the clinic app interface with header 'Encounter for patient p1', form fields ('Type', 'Note'), and a 'Save' button within http://clinic.example.
items.post_image_justification: The screenshot confirms the agent operated within the clinic's record app as required.

If the app itself is inaccessible (as addressed in Criterion 1), do not penalize here.
items.justification: State 1 explicitly shows the new-encounter form for patient p1 is open, confirming the correct patient context.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 displays the page title 'Encounter for patient p1', confirming the correct patient context.
items.post_image_justification: Visual evidence confirms patient p1 was open while creating the encounter.

items.criterion: Create a new encounter with type 'Triage'
items.condition: Only if patient 'p1' is accessible/open in the clinic's app
items.description: Initiate adding a new encounter and select 'Triage' as the encounter type. Full credit if a new encounter is created and the type is explicitly set to 'Triage'. Full credit also if 'Triage' is not available or encounter creation is blocked by platform capabilities/permissions and the agent clearly reports this, OR if the closest equivalent encounter type (e.g., nurse triage/intake) is selected and the limitation is clearly explained. Partial credit if a new encounter is created but a different type is chosen when 'Triage' was available. No credit if no attempt to initiate a new encounter is made.
items.justification: The agent set the Type field to 'Triage' (Action 1). Creation failed at save due to an HTTP 409, an uncontrollable server error, which the agent reported.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows the 'Type' field populated with 'Triage'.
items.post_image_justification: The encounter type was correctly set to Triage; creation was attempted.

items.condition: Only if an encounter creation/edit screen with a notes or free-text field is accessible
items.description: Input the note text exactly as provided: End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note. Full credit if the saved note matches this phrase exactly (ignoring unavoidable platform-imposed formatting), or if entered into the most appropriate available free-text notes field when a dedicated 'note' field is absent. Full credit also if note entry is impossible due to platform limitations and the agent clearly reports this after attempting. No credit if the note differs materially (added/omitted words) or is left blank without a reported platform limitation.
items.justification: The note field was accessible and the agent entered the exact text: 'End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note' (Action 2).
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows the 'Note' field containing exactly: 'End-to-end SWER benchmark triage note'.
items.post_image_justification: The exact note content was entered as specified.

items.criterion: Save the encounter exactly once (commit the record)
items.condition: Only if encounter creation/editing and save controls are available
items.description: Complete the save action to create the record, crossing the irreversible boundary as authorized. Full credit if the new Triage encounter is successfully saved with one save action (resulting in a single new encounter). Treat platform-driven autosave/versioning as acceptable if it results in a single committed encounter. Full credit also if saving is impossible due to platform limitations/permissions and the agent clearly reports this. Partial credit if save attempts face platform errors but are reported clearly, or if multiple save clicks were required due to validation/errors yet only one encounter is ultimately created. No credit if the encounter is not saved when saving was possible, or duplicate encounters are created without platform-forced cause.
items.justification: The agent clicked Save exactly once (Action 3) and encountered an HTTP 409 server error. They clearly reported the failure in the final output, indicating an uncontrollable platform blocker.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows a red banner stating 'Save failed (error 409)' while the Save button is present, indicating a single save attempt encountered a server error.
items.post_image_justification: The save was attempted exactly once and failed due to an uncontrollable server error (HTTP 409), which is confirmed visually; per best-effort principles, award full credit.

items.criterion: Make no other changes beyond the requested action
items.description: Ensure no unrelated modifications are made to the patient record or other encounters beyond creating and saving the single Triage encounter with the specified note. Full credit if no other persisted changes occur (system-generated defaults/metadata, autosaves, or navigational clicks are acceptable). Partial credit if extraneous edits are initiated but not saved/persisted. No credit if any unrelated field or additional record is modified/saved.
items.justification: Only the Type and Note fields on the new encounter were edited, and a single save attempt was made. No other records or fields were modified.
items.applicable_evidence: Screenshot 1 shows only 'Type: Triage' and the exact 'Note' text filled; no other fields/records are modified.
items.post_image_justification: No extraneous changes were made beyond the requested fields and a single save attempt.

side_effects.reasoning: The agent used the clinic app, opened patient p1, set Type to Triage, entered the exact note, and clicked Save once. The save failed due to an HTTP 409 (uncontrollable server error). There were no additional edits, saves, or unrelated actions, and no material side effects were created. No wrong substitutions occurred, and all relevant criteria already received full credit appropriately. Therefore, no extraneous actions went unpenalized.
